transcript.content:
hey, i'm berry

tell me your dream, however it comes back to you. bits and pieces are fine

hey berry. ok so the bit that stuck with me most is at the end. my grandmother's kitchen table turned into a small wooden boat and she told me to get in, and it floated out the door onto the street, except the street was a river now. my little brother was waving at me from the bank holding this lantern that was glowing blue. then i woke up

the table just becoming a boat, and the street quietly turning into a river… i love that

when she told you to get in and you floated out the door, how did that feel?

honestly i don't really remember how it felt, the dream doesn't give me much on that. i just remember getting in because she told me to, and then floating out. it all seemed kind of normal while it was happening, like dreams do

that's fair, dreams do that. it all just seems normal while you're in it

when your brother was waving from the bank, were you seeing him through your own eyes from the boat, or was it more like watching the whole thing from somewhere outside?
i don't really remember that either tbh. i know i was sitting in the boat and he was on the bank waving, but whether i was seeing it from my own eyes or from outside, no idea

that's fine, doesn't matter

so here's what i've got. you were at your grandmother's, and her kitchen table turned into a small wooden boat. she told you to get in, so you did, and it floated out the door onto the street, except the street was a river now. your little brother was on the bank, waving at you and holding a lantern that was glowing blue. it all seemed kind of normal while it was happening. and then you woke up

did i get that right, or did i miss anything?

yeah that's right for that part. one thing, the street it floated onto was the same one the bus had been on earlier. there was more before the kitchen too, it started on a night bus with my brother going home in the rain, and then i was suddenly in my grandmother's kitchen in the morning. there were neighbours squeezed in the doorway watching too

oh, so it started before the kitchen. you were on a night bus with your brother, going home in the rain, and then suddenly you were in your grandmother's kitchen and it was morning. neighbours were squeezed in the doorway watching, and when the boat floated out, the river was the same street the bus had been on earlier

have i got that part right now?

yeah that's it. on the bus my brother was holding the lantern too, it was just a paper one with a candle in it then, it only turned blue in the kitchen. and my grandmother was at the stove making tea, her hair was really white, whiter than i've ever seen it

oh, so the lantern was there from the start. on the bus your brother was holding a paper one with a candle in it, and it only turned blue once you were in the kitchen. and your grandmother was at the stove making tea, her hair whiter than you've ever seen it

have i got that right?

yeah that's right. couple of small things on the bus, it was almost empty, just the driver and an old woman knitting at the back. and the street lights outside the window were kind of melting into long orange ribbons. oh and the neighbours, there were maybe eight or ten of them, just watching quietly

the street lights melting into long orange ribbons outside the window… and eight or ten neighbours just watching quietly. i've got it

would you like to see your dream drawn?
yeah i'd like that

ok, a few ways it could be drawn

soft watercolour, gentle and a bit wet, like a memory that went soft while you weren't looking. or an old storybook painting, like a page from a bedtime story where impossible things happen politely and everyone just watches. or soft coloured pencil, quiet and hand-made, like someone drew it the second they woke so it wouldn't slip away. or a real photo, just how it looked to you, normal even when the street's a river

which feels closest, or is there another way you'd picture it?
the real photo one i think. it all looked normal to me, even the river

ok, let's start with your grandmother

i'm picturing her just as herself, older, with that really white hair, whiter than you've ever seen it. i'm guessing at the clothes, something comfy for around the house, maybe a cardigan or an apron

anything different from how you see her, or leave it to me?
yeah that sounds right. i don't remember what she was wearing so go with your guess. she was at the stove making tea when i first saw her if that helps

ok, i'm sketching your grandmother, the driver, the old woman, the night bus, her kitchen, the lantern and the kitchen table now. it'll show up on the right

and your little brother, i'm picturing him younger than you, in a rain jacket. those two bits are just my guesses

anything different, or leave him to me?
yeah younger is right, he's my little brother. i don't remember what he was wearing so the rain jacket's fine, go with it. just make sure he's got the lantern, paper one with the candle on the bus

got it, he'll have the lantern. a paper one with a candle on the bus, then glowing blue once you're in the kitchen

so your little brother's younger than you, in a rain jacket, holding that lantern, and waving from the bank at the end

is that him, or is anything different?
yeah that's him. he's still holding the blue lantern when he's waving from the bank, so keep that in

ok, i'm sketching your little brother now, blue lantern and all. he'll show up on the right

and the street, i'm picturing it as the same one from the bus, just an ordinary street, except it's a river now, the water sitting right where the road should be. i'm guessing it's in morning light, since you'd just come from the kitchen

anything different, or leave it to me?
yeah that sounds right. i don't remember what the light was like when i was in the boat, so morning's a good guess, go with it

ok, sketching the street now, it'll show up on the right

and since you're in it too, i'll draw you as well. do you want to be drawn as you are, and tell me a little about yourself, or should i just imagine you?
just imagine me, that's fine. the dream doesn't really say anything about what i looked like, so go with whatever you think

ok, i'll imagine you. sketching you now

everything's being sketched and it'll all show up on the right over the next minute or two. once it's there, just tell me if anything looks wrong
ok they're all up, they look right to me. nice seeing it all together like that

it's nice seeing them all together, isn't it

does it look the way you remember it, or does anything feel off?
yeah it looks how i remember it. nothing feels off to me

good, i'm glad it all looks how you remember it

i'll draw the moments of your dream now, in order, starting on the night bus and ending with your brother waving from the bank. each one carries on from the ones before it, and they'll show up on the right as they're ready
ok cool, i can see the first two, they look right so far. i'll wait for the rest

the bus and those street lights melting into long orange ribbons, that's how it started

the rest carry on from these two, so i'll draw them once you tell me these look right or what to change. do they look the way you remember?
yeah they look right, the bus and the orange ribbons outside the window, that's how it was. go ahead with the rest

good, that's how it started then

i'm drawing the rest now, the kitchen, the boat, the river and your brother on the bank. they'll show up on the right soon
ok the third one's up, looks right. i'll wait for the others

the kitchen in the morning, her at the stove with that white hair

the boat and the river carry on from this one, so nothing you'd change in the kitchen before i go on?
nope, the kitchen looks right. as long as my brother's in there with the lantern glowing blue and the neighbours are in the doorway, go ahead

good, the kitchen's done then

your brother with the lantern glowing blue, the neighbours squeezed in the doorway, the boat and the river are all coming. the other three will show up on the right soon
ok the fourth one's up, looks right. i'll wait for the last two

the table turned into a little wooden boat, right there in her kitchen

anything you'd change in this one before the last two?
nope that one looks right. go ahead with the last two

good, the boat's right then

the last two are coming, floating out onto the river and your brother waving from the bank. they'll show up on the right soon
ok the fifth one's up, looks right. just waiting on the last one with my brother on the bank

you in the boat, floating out the door onto the river where the street used to be

good, that one's right then. the last one's coming, your brother on the bank with the blue lantern, waving. it'll show up on the right soon
ok cool, i'll wait for that one

it's on its way. your brother on the bank, waving, with the blue lantern

it'll show up on the right soon
oh the last one's up. that's him on the bank waving with the blue lantern, looks right. that's pretty much the whole dream, start to finish. thanks berry

thank you for sharing it with me

a paper lantern on a night bus that turned blue in your grandmother's kitchen, and your little brother still holding it on the bank while you floated off down the street that became a river. that's a lovely one to have all together, start to finish

moments.action: The dreamer rides the almost empty night bus home in the rain with their little brother, who holds a paper lantern with a candle in it. The driver is at the front and an old woman knits at the back.
Outside the bus window, the street lights melt into long orange ribbons in the rain.
Suddenly it is morning in the grandmother's kitchen. She is making tea at the stove, her hair whiter than ever, and the brother's lantern now glows blue.
The kitchen table has become a small wooden boat, and the grandmother tells the dreamer to get in while the neighbours watch quietly from the doorway.
The dreamer sits in the boat as it floats out the door onto the street, which is now a river.
From the bank, the little brother waves to the dreamer in the boat while holding the lantern glowing blue.

key_moment.evidence: hey berry. ok so the bit that stuck with me most is at the end. my grandmother's kitchen table turned into a small wooden boat and she told me to get in, and it floated out the door onto the street, except the street was a river now. my little brother was waving at me from the bank holding this lantern that was glowing blue. then i woke up
